A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CADE dataset and human-annotation and LLM studies. Their main text, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses of 2,094 YouTube comments annotated by 57 participants, including agreement, moral-profile clustering and evaluations of six LLMs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports joint label distributions, corpus label counts and participant-feedback findings.

M1.justification: The annotation scheme, MFQ-based moral profiles, agglomerative clustering and zero-shot LLM prompting remain unchanged. Expanded explanations of participant engagement do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six celebrity events, YouTube corpus, annotator population and annotation tasks. The checkout questionnaire and its 33 responses already appear in v1; v2 newly reports findings from that existing coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 2 retain OLMo 7B, BLOOMZ 3B, DeepSeek R1 1.5B, OPT-IML 1.3B, Llama 3.2 3B and Ministral 8B. Added literature comparisons do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The added Table 3 analysis conditions stance percentages on unacceptability level and includes only instances labeled for both tasks, explicitly excluding 350 annotations. Existing study protocols remain unchanged. Administering the moral questionnaire after annotation is proposed only for future work.

E4.justification: v2 adds a descriptive analysis of the relationship between stance and unacceptability (Table 3), examples covering all 12 label combinations (Table 7), and participant-feedback findings about questionnaire influence and interpretation difficulties (Appendix D).

E5.justification: Pearson tests, chi-squared testing at p < 0.05, and agreement means and standard deviations across annotation samples are retained. v2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run reporting, uncertainty intervals or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports Attack shares of 15.97% at unacceptability level 1 and 74.61% at level 4 (Table 3), label counts (Appendix E), and eight respondents reporting questionnaire influence (Appendix D). Existing Table 2, Figure 2 and sample-level agreement values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version adds formal theoretical results or proofs. Questionnaire scoring and clustering mathematics remain unchanged; expanded explanations of moral foundations and an additional supporting citation are conceptual clarifications.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same claims: CADE enables studying morality-related disagreement, judgments depend on the event, and LLMs align differently with annotator groups. Expanded future-work plans do not change these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 qualifies the earlier stance–unacceptability orthogonality interpretation by distinguishing the aggregate association from celebrity-level patterns, and softens the Rowling explanation into an inference. v2 also acknowledges questionnaire influence, bias from disclosing research objectives, and linguistic/cultural interpretation difficulties.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the promised future dataset release with a concrete repository link and adds a checkout-response CSV link. It newly documents collected metadata, immediate username anonymization and metadata exclusion from the released corpus. Model identifiers, prompts and GPU details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Haidt and Graham (2007), Landis and Koch (1977), Sachdeva et al. (2022), and Passonneau and Carpenter (2014), supporting moral-foundation interpretation and annotation-agreement discussion. The principal related-work framing and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local language corrections, expands explanations of moral foundations and participation, and adds author contributions and acknowledgements. Appendix D is expanded and new Appendices E–F precede the retained LLM details, now Appendix G. The main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 7, expands the captions of Figures 1–2, and reflows existing figures and appendix tables. The original graphics are retained. Appendix pagination leaves the final fragment of the LLM prompt alone on page 15.

improvement.justification: The joint-label analysis, annotated examples and participant-feedback findings make the existing evidence and potential biases easier to assess. Access information and metadata disclosures improve transparency. These gains outweigh minor pagination defects, but the core experiments remain unchanged and the newly acknowledged priming concerns are not experimentally resolved.
